qs.ours: + By Calmet and others. The authorities on this question are much opposed to each other. In support of the opinion that Judas was not at the Lord's supper, see Doddridge^e, Guyse, and others. That Judas was at the Lord's table is argued by Lightfoot, at great length; also by Whitby, Dr Sam. Clarke, Kidder in his Demonstr. of the Messiah, iii. 3, Henry, &c. Macknight thinks that John xiii. describes the paschal supper, but that Judas was at the Lord's supper notwithstanding. Scott also holds John xiii. to relate to the passover evening, but seems quite undecided as to whether Judas was a communicant. Poole's Synopsis may also be consulted.
